evidence.claim: The Pequot Trail passed from state highway to town road and back.
evidence.quote: Route 84 was relocated in 1935 to the Providence-New London Turnpike, and the Pequot Trail reverted to town control. In 1963, the current Route 234 was taken over by the state again as unsigned State Road 645.

evidence.claim: Route 234 crosses central Stonington from Old Mystic toward Pawcatuck, carrying the name Pequot Trail for its entire length.
evidence.quote: Route 234 is known as the Pequot Trail for its entire length.

evidence.claim: The drive heads southeast before turning east, passing over Interstate 95 along the way.
evidence.quote: It heads southeast across central Stonington, crossing over I-95 without an intersection after 2.4 miles (3.9 km), before turning east

evidence.claim: Only the section from the western end to North Main Street is designated a state scenic road.
evidence.quote: The section of Route 234 from the western terminus to the intersection with North Main Street is designated as a state scenic road.

evidence.claim: The trail entered the numbered state highway system in 1932 as the eastern half of Route 84.
evidence.quote: Modern Route 234 (Pequot Trail) was first designated as a numbered state highway in the 1932 state highway renumbering. It was originally the eastern half of the newly established Route 84 (now modern Route 184).

evidence.claim: When Route 84 moved to the Providence-New London Turnpike in 1935, the Pequot Trail returned to town control.
evidence.quote: Route 84 was relocated in 1935 to the Providence-New London Turnpike, and the Pequot Trail reverted to town control.

evidence.claim: The state took it back in 1963 as unsigned State Road 645; the Route 234 number followed in 1987.
evidence.quote: In 1963, the current Route 234 was taken over by the state again as unsigned State Road 645.  It was redesignated as Route 234 in 1987.

evidence.claim: Begin at Route 27 in Old Mystic.
evidence.quote: Route 234 begins at an intersection with Route 27 in the Old Mystic section of the town of Stonington.

evidence.claim: The first I-95 crossing, 2.4 miles along, has no intersection; another mile brings the road east to an interchange.
evidence.quote: crossing over I-95 without an intersection after 2.4 miles (3.9 km), before turning east to an interchange with I-95 (at Exit 104) after another mile.

evidence.claim: Beyond that, Route 234 continues east for 3.5 miles to US 1 in Pawcatuck.
evidence.quote: Route 234 then continues east another 3.5 miles (5.6 km) to end at an intersection with US 1 in the Pawcatuck section of Stonington.

evidence.claim: Old Mystic straddles Groton and Stonington, while the Pequot Trail begins on the Stonington side at Route 27.
evidence.quote: Old Mystic is a village and census-designated place (CDP) located in the towns of Groton and Stonington Connecticut.

evidence.claim: At 39 Main Street, the former Mystic Bank gives the village a connection to shipbuilding: local businessmen founded the bank in 1833 to serve shipbuilders and the surrounding rural area.
evidence.quote: The Mystic Bank was founded in 1833 by a consortium of local businessmen as a service to the local shipbuilding community and the surrounding rural areas.

evidence.claim: The business expanded into its brick building in 1856.
evidence.quote: The bank flourished, and was able to build this building in 1856 to accommodate its expanded business.

evidence.claim: After the bank closed, Stonington acquired the building for district meetings and voting.
evidence.quote: The town of Stonington acquired the building soon afterward, and used it as a district meeting hall and polling place.

evidence.claim: Its three-bay front has a pedimented gable and round-arched recesses.
evidence.quote: The main facade is three bays wide, topped by a pedimented gable.  Each bay is set in a round-arch recess

evidence.claim: At 39 Main Street
evidence.quote: The Mystic Bank is a historic commercial building at 39 Main Street

evidence.claim: the Pequot Trail begins on the Stonington side at Route 27.
evidence.quote: Route 234 begins at an intersection with Route 27 in the Old Mystic section of the town of Stonington.

evidence.claim: The Pequot Trail crosses above I-95 2.4 miles from its start, without an intersection.
evidence.quote: crossing over I-95 without an intersection after 2.4 miles (3.9 km)

evidence.claim: This is a crossing rather than an entrance to the interstate: Route 234 continues southeast before turning east toward an interchange another mile along.
evidence.quote: It heads southeast across central Stonington, crossing over I-95 without an intersection after 2.4 miles (3.9 km), before turning east to an interchange with I-95 (at Exit 104) after another mile.

evidence.claim: Stonington Cemetery lies at North Main Street and Route 1, beyond the trail itself.
evidence.quote: Stonington Cemetery is a historic cemetery at North Main Street and Route 1 in Stonington, Connecticut.

evidence.claim: Its oldest legible marker dates to 1754, when this was the Chesebrough family burying ground.
evidence.quote: The cemetery was begun at least as early as 1754, the date on its oldest legible grave marker.  It was at the time the family cemetery of the Chesebrough family

evidence.claim: The Phelps family acquired the cemetery in 1792 and allowed others to be buried here; incorporation in 1849 formalized its public use.
evidence.quote: the cemetery was sold to the Phelpses in 1792, and became locally known as the Phelps Burying Ground.  The Phelpses allowed others to use the cemetery, and its use as a public cemetery was formalized with the incorporation of the Stonington Cemetery Corporation in 1849.

evidence.claim: Three nineteenth-century expansions left the oldest sections in the western third.
evidence.quote: The cemetery has undergone three major expansions, all in the 19th century; the oldest sections of the cemetery are in its western third.

evidence.claim: Stone walls and fencing surround rectangular sections divided by paved and gravel roadways.
evidence.quote: It is ringed by a combination of stone walls and fencing, each of varying ages, with the main gate facing Main Street.  It is divided into generally rectangular sections, with roadways, some paved and some gravel, defining their perimeters and providing circulation.

evidence.claim: Route 234 crosses central Stonington from Old Mystic toward Pawcatuck
evidence.quote: Route 234 is a state highway in southeastern Connecticut, running entirely within the town of Stonington. It connects the Old Mystic section of town with the village of Pawcatuck.

evidence.claim: its brick building
evidence.quote: It is a modest single-story brick building

evidence.claim: The building rests on a granite foundation beneath its gabled roof.
evidence.quote: It is a modest single-story brick building, with a gabled roof and granite foundation.

evidence.claim: Its enlargements came in 1849, 1864 and 1888, with each section following the cemetery fashions of its time.
evidence.quote: At that time it underwent its first enlargement, with further increases occurring in 1864 and 1888.  Each section was laid out according to practices that were fashionable at the time.

evidence.claim: The cemetery’s oldest sections occupy its western third.
evidence.quote: the oldest sections of the cemetery are in its western third.

Mystic Bank cache conflicts on closure year (1884/1887) and current use (offices/museum); omitted both.
